about: How Claude scores each job against the master CV. Total = sum of criteria (max 100), then hard gates cap it. Every criterion must be scored only from facts in cv/master_cv.md and the advert text; when the advert doesn't say, use the 'not stated' rule.

criteria.label: Role match
criteria.question: How close is the job to the roles in target_roles?

anchors.20: Same job family as a target role, and the day-to-day tasks match what the CV shows (e.g. BA role, CV shows requirements/process/KPI work).
anchors.12: Adjacent family (e.g. data analyst vs business analyst) or the title fits but half the duties are elsewhere (sales, engineering).
anchors.5: Analyst in name only; most duties are outside the target roles.
anchors.0: Different career track (developer, sales, trades, senior management).

criteria.label: Skills & tools
criteria.question: What share of the advert's required skills and tools does the CV show with evidence?
criteria.method: List the advert's must-have skills (count 2) and nice-to-haves (count 1). Score = 25 x (evidenced weight / total weight), rounded. 'Evidenced' means the CV names the skill in a role, project or degree, not just a skills list; a skills-list-only mention counts half.
criteria.not_stated: If the advert lists no skills, score 15 and lower confidence.

criteria.label: Experience level
criteria.question: Does the required experience match Dhruv's level (graduate/early career)?

anchors.15: Graduate, entry level, 0-1 years, or no requirement stated.
anchors.11: 1-2 years, or 'some experience' that the CV's roles/internships/projects cover.
anchors.0: 5+ years or a senior/lead/manager title (also triggers the experience gate).

criteria.label: Qualifications
criteria.question: Does the CV meet the degree, certificate or licence requirements?

anchors.10: Meets all stated requirements, or exceeds them (e.g. master's where a degree is asked).
anchors.6: Meets the essential ones but not the desirable ones.
anchors.2: Missing an essential qualification that can be explained or is in progress.
anchors.0: Missing a mandatory licence, chartership or clearance.

criteria.label: Industry fit
criteria.question: Has Dhruv worked or studied in this sector (property, finance, retail, public sector, energy...)?

anchors.10: Direct experience in the same sector.
anchors.6: Related sector, or dissertation/projects in it.
anchors.3: No link, but the advert says sector experience isn't needed.
anchors.0: Advert requires sector experience the CV doesn't have.

criteria.label: Visa & salary
criteria.question: Can this job realistically sponsor a Skilled Worker visa?
criteria.method: Register: licensed Skilled Worker = 4, possible/recruiter with licensed end client = 2, not found = 0. Advert: offers sponsorship = 3, silent = 1, says no = 0. Salary: meets £41,700 = 3, meets £33,400 new-entrant = 2, unknown = 1, below = 0. Skip this criterion's penalty (score 10) if visa.needs_sponsorship is false.

criteria.label: Location & terms
criteria.question: Does location, work pattern and contract suit the profile's locations?

anchors.5: In a preferred location or remote/hybrid UK, permanent full time.
anchors.3: Needs a move or long commute, or a fixed-term contract over 6 months.
anchors.0: Outside the UK, very short contract, or self-employed/commission only.

criteria.label: Chance of hearing back
criteria.question: How likely is an application to be seen?
criteria.method: Start at 5. Posted more than 3 days ago -1. Easy Apply (high volume) -1. Recruiter with the client unnamed -1. Very large brand graduate scheme -1. Minimum 0.

gates.rule: Advert requires 5+ years or a senior/lead/manager level
Advert says it cannot sponsor, or applicants must already have the right to work, while visa.needs_sponsorship is true
Employer-stated salary (not a Glassdoor estimate) tops out below the £33,400 new-entrant rate while visa.needs_sponsorship is true
Advert requires a licence, chartership or security clearance the CV doesn't show (SC/DV clearance usually needs 5 years UK residence)
Employer not on the sponsor register, not a recruiter, and the advert doesn't offer sponsorship, while visa.needs_sponsorship is true

confidence.high: Full advert read and scored against the uploaded master CV.
confidence.medium: Advert read, but scored against a provisional profile (no master CV yet), or the advert is vague.
confidence.low: Advert couldn't be loaded; scored from the title only.
